claims.statement: For a challenge P uniform among nonidentity G1 points and an independent uniform z in GT, the serial 20-adding distinguished-point walk in proof.md returns Q in G2 with e(P,Q)=z, including Q=infinity when z=1. Under the single random-mapping heuristic stated in proof.md, the success probability is at least 0.5. The same proof charges at most 2^128.191581 target-group-operation equivalents in total, including preprocessing, distinguished-point storage, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^118.928545 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^13.356590 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in the total. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. One processor is used; work is not divided by orbit size or by a processor count. This is a classical cold attack and an analytic generic accounting control, not a claim of novelty or of a practical break.

experiments.purpose: On a toy cyclic group, check that a 20-adding walk with every branch incrementing the z-exponent recovers every discrete log from a distinguished-point collision. This does not establish production mixing, memory or Fp12 costs.
